grades.quote: The RISC-V CPU raises a page-fault exception when a virtual address is used that has no mapping in the page table, or has a mapping whose PTE_V flag is clear, or a mapping whose permission bits (PTE_R, PTE_W, PTE_X, PTE_U) forbid the operation being attempted.
grades.reason: Explains why accessing an unmapped page triggers a detectable fault, but does not connect this to kernel-stack overflow.

grades.quote: Xv6 performs a few: mapping the same memory (a trampoline page) in several address spaces, guarding kernel and user stacks with an unmapped page, and allocating user heap memory lazily.
grades.reason: Confirms xv6 uses unmapped pages to guard stacks, but does not explain how they detect overflow.
Exercises about trap mappings and register storage do not explain guard pages or stack-overflow detection.
